DEVICE STATUS MONITORING - STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
=========================================================

Purpose: To establish standardized procedures for monitoring and checking device operational status across the network infrastructure.

SCOPE
-----
This SOP applies to all network devices including:
- ONT (Optical Network Terminals)
- Routers (Core, Edge, Branch)
- Switches
- Firewalls
- Load Balancers

DEVICE STATUS CATEGORIES
-------------------------

ONLINE
- Device is reachable and responding
- All interfaces operational
- No critical alarms
- Performance within normal parameters

OFFLINE
- Device not responding to management queries
- Complete loss of connectivity
- Requires immediate investigation

DEGRADED
- Device responding but with issues
- One or more interfaces down
- Performance below normal thresholds
- Warning alarms present

MAINTENANCE
- Device intentionally taken offline
- Scheduled maintenance window
- Configuration changes in progress

MONITORING METHODS
------------------

1. AUTOMATED MONITORING
   - SNMP polling (5-minute intervals)
   - Syslog collection
   - NetFlow analysis
   - Health check scripts

2. MANUAL STATUS CHECKS
   - Command-line interface queries
   - Web management interface
   - Physical inspection when needed

STATUS CHECK PROCEDURES
-----------------------

FOR ONT DEVICES:
1. Verify device responds to ping
2. Check optical signal levels
3. Review connection status
4. Validate VLAN assignment
5. Check for CRC errors
6. Verify configured speed matches actual

FOR ROUTER DEVICES:
1. Check management IP reachability
2. Verify routing protocol status
3. Review interface states
4. Check CPU and memory utilization
5. Validate BGP/OSPF neighbor status
6. Review error counters

THRESHOLD ALERTS
----------------

CRITICAL (Immediate Response Required):
- Device completely offline
- Multiple interface failures
- CPU > 90% for 10+ minutes
- Memory > 95%
- Temperature > 85°C

WARNING (Response Within 1 Hour):
- Single interface down
- CPU > 70% for 30+ minutes
- Memory > 80%
- Elevated error rates
- Temperature > 75°C

INFO (Review During Business Hours):
- Minor configuration changes needed
- Firmware updates available
- Performance optimization opportunities

RESPONSE PROCEDURES
-------------------

When a device shows OFFLINE status:

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (0-5 minutes):
1. Verify monitoring system accuracy
2. Attempt to ping device
3. Check for maintenance windows
4. Review recent change logs

ESCALATION (5-15 minutes):
1. Attempt console connection
2. Check physical connectivity
3. Review power status
4. Contact data center tech if needed

RESOLUTION (15+ minutes):
1. Diagnose root cause
2. Apply fix (reboot, config change, etc.)
3. Verify return to ONLINE status
4. Document incident details
5. Update monitoring system

REPORTING
---------

Daily Status Report:
- Total devices monitored
- Devices currently offline
- Devices in degraded state
- Devices under maintenance

Weekly Summary:
- Uptime statistics per device type
- Incident trends
- Top 10 devices by downtime
- Recommendations for improvements

COMMON STATUS CHECK COMMANDS
-----------------------------

ONT Status:
- show ont status
- show optical-levels
- show vlan-assignment

Router Status (Cisco):
- show interfaces status
- show ip route summary
- show processes cpu
- show memory statistics
- show version
- show inventory

Router Status (Juniper):
- show chassis hardware
- show interfaces terse
- show route summary
- show system uptime
- show chassis routing-engine

BEST PRACTICES
--------------

1. Always verify status from multiple sources
2. Don't rely solely on automated monitoring
3. Document all status checks
4. Establish baseline performance metrics
5. Regularly review and update thresholds
6. Maintain accurate device inventory
7. Keep runbooks updated

ESCALATION PATH
---------------

Level 1: Automated Monitoring System
  |
  v
Level 2: Network Operations Center (NOC)
  |
  v
Level 3: Network Engineering Team
  |
  v
Level 4: Vendor Technical Support
  |
  v
Level 5: Emergency Response Team

RELATED DOCUMENTS
-----------------
- Device Registration Procedures
- Incident Response Plan
- Change Management Policy
- Network Architecture Guide

REVISION HISTORY
----------------
Version 1.0 - Initial Release
Version 1.1 - Added threshold values
Version 1.2 - Updated escalation procedures

Contact: Network Operations - netops@company.com

# ONT Registration Procedure

## Overview
This document outlines the standard operating procedure for registering Optical Network Terminal (ONT) devices in the network management system.

## Prerequisites
- ONT device ID
- Physical location information
- Network VLAN assignment
- Connection speed requirements

## Registration Steps

### Step 1: Verify Device Information
Before registration, ensure you have:
- **Device ID**: Unique identifier (e.g., ONT-001, ONT-002)
- **Location**: Full physical address (Building, Floor, Room)
- **VLAN**: Assigned VLAN ID (typically 100-999)
- **Speed**: Connection speed (100Mbps, 1000Mbps, or 10Gbps)

### Step 2: Register Device
Use the registration system to add the ONT:
1. Access the device management interface
2. Select "Register New ONT"
3. Enter device information
4. Verify VLAN availability
5. Confirm registration

### Step 3: Configuration
After registration, the ONT requires initial configuration:
- **VLAN Configuration**: Set VLAN ID per network design
- **Speed Configuration**: Configure link speed
- **Quality of Service**: Apply QoS policies
- **Security Settings**: Enable security features

### Step 4: Testing
Perform the following tests:
1. Link connectivity test
2. Speed test (verify configured speed)
3. VLAN isolation test
4. End-to-end connectivity test

## Troubleshooting

### Device Not Responding
- Check physical connections
- Verify power supply
- Check VLAN configuration
- Review network logs

### Speed Issues
- Verify configured speed matches capability
- Check for network congestion
- Review QoS settings
- Test with different endpoints

### VLAN Issues
- Confirm VLAN exists in network
- Verify VLAN tagging
- Check switch port configuration
- Review VLAN routing

## Best Practices
- Always document the exact location
- Use standardized naming conventions (ONT-XXX)
- Keep VLAN assignments organized
- Perform immediate testing after registration
- Update inventory system promptly

## Example Registration
```
Device ID: ONT-1234
Location: Building A - Floor 2 - Room 201
VLAN: 150
Speed: 1000Mbps
Status: Active
```

## Contact Information
For assistance with ONT registration:
- Network Operations: netops@company.com
- Technical Support: support@company.com
- Emergency: 1-800-TECH-911

# SOP Documents Directory

Place your Standard Operating Procedures and other documents in this directory.

## Supported File Formats

- **PDF Files**: `.pdf`
- **Microsoft Word**: `.docx`, `.doc` 
- **Microsoft Excel**: `.xlsx`, `.xls`
- **Text Files**: `.txt`
- **Markdown**: `.md`

## Usage

1. Add your document files to this directory
2. Run: `python main.py update` (will automatically use this SOP directory)
3. Start the chatbot: `python main.py web` or `python main.py chat`

The system will recursively process all supported files in this directory and its subdirectories.

## Example Structure

```
SOP/
├── policies/
│   ├── security_policy.pdf
│   └── data_retention.docx
├── procedures/
│   ├── incident_response.md
│   └── backup_procedures.txt
└── guidelines/
    ├── coding_standards.pdf
    └── review_process.xlsx
```

# Router Management Guide

## Overview
Comprehensive guide for managing router devices including registration, configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

## Router Types
Our network uses the following router types:
- **Cisco ASR Series**: Core routers for main data centers
- **Juniper MX Series**: Edge routers for distribution
- **Cisco ISR Series**: Branch office routers
- **Arista 7000 Series**: Data center switching/routing

## Registration Procedure

### Initial Registration
When adding a new router to the network:

1. **Device Information**
   - Device ID (e.g., ROUTER-001)
   - Model and manufacturer
   - Firmware version
   - Serial number
   - Purchase date

2. **Location Details**
   - Data center or site name
   - Rack location
   - Physical connections
   - Power circuit information

3. **Network Configuration**
   - Management IP address
   - Routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, etc.)
   - Interface assignments
   - Access control lists

### Configuration Management

#### Standard Configuration Template
```
hostname [ROUTER-ID]
!
ip routing
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
  description Uplink to Core
  ip address [IP] [MASK]
  no shutdown
!
router bgp [ASN]
  neighbor [IP] remote-as [ASN]
!
```

#### Firmware Management
- Check current firmware: `show version`
- Recommended versions:
  - Cisco ASR: v15.6 or later
  - Juniper MX: v18.4 or later
  - Cisco ISR: v16.12 or later

### Monitoring and Status Checks

#### Health Check Commands
```bash
# Cisco
show ip interface brief
show ip route
show processes cpu
show memory

# Juniper
show interfaces terse
show route summary
show chassis routing-engine
```

#### Key Metrics to Monitor
- CPU utilization (< 70% normal)
- Memory usage (< 80% normal)
- Interface errors
- BGP session status
- Temperature sensors

### Configuration Push Procedure

When pushing new configurations:

1. **Backup Current Config**
   ```
   copy running-config backup-config-[DATE]
   ```

2. **Apply New Configuration**
   - Review changes in staging environment
   - Schedule maintenance window
   - Apply configuration during low-traffic period
   - Verify changes immediately

3. **Validation**
   - Test all routing protocols
   - Verify interface status
   - Check BGP/OSPF neighbors
   - Perform connectivity tests

### Troubleshooting

#### Router Not Responding
- Check physical power
- Verify console connectivity
- Review system logs
- Check for software crashes

#### Routing Issues
- Verify routing protocol configuration
- Check neighbor relationships
- Review routing tables
- Validate access lists

#### Performance Problems
- Check CPU and memory
- Review interface statistics
- Analyze traffic patterns
- Look for routing loops

#### BGP Issues
- Verify neighbor configuration
- Check AS numbers
- Review route filters
- Validate MD5 authentication

### Maintenance Procedures

#### Regular Maintenance Tasks
- **Weekly**: Review logs and alerts
- **Monthly**: Firmware updates check
- **Quarterly**: Performance review
- **Annually**: Hardware refresh evaluation

#### Emergency Procedures
1. Isolate affected router
2. Fail over to redundant path
3. Document issue details
4. Contact vendor support if needed
5. Apply fix or replacement
6. Test thoroughly before returning to service

## Best Practices

### Configuration Management
- Always use version control for configs
- Document all changes
- Test in lab before production
- Maintain rollback configurations

### Security
- Change default passwords immediately
- Enable AAA authentication
- Use encrypted management protocols
- Regularly update ACLs

### Documentation
- Keep network diagrams updated
- Document all connections
- Maintain runbook procedures
- Record configuration changes

## Emergency Contacts
- Network Operations Center: noc@company.com
- Cisco TAC: 1-800-553-2447
- Juniper JTAC: 1-888-314-5822
- Internal Emergency: ext. 9111

# IT Security Policy

## Overview
This document outlines the IT security policies and procedures for our organization.

## Password Requirements
- Passwords must be at least 12 characters long
- Must contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters
- Passwords must be changed every 90 days
- Cannot reuse the last 12 passwords

## Access Control
- All employees must use multi-factor authentication
- Access rights should follow the principle of least privilege
- Regular access reviews must be conducted quarterly

## Data Protection
- All sensitive data must be encrypted in transit and at rest
- Personal data must be handled according to GDPR requirements
- Data backups must be performed daily and tested monthly

## Incident Response
- All security incidents must be reported within 1 hour
- The incident response team consists of IT, Security, and Management
- Post-incident reviews must be conducted within 48 hours

## Training
- Security awareness training is required annually
- New employees must complete security training within 30 days
- Phishing simulation exercises are conducted monthly

vectors.content:
The device supports:
Multiple fiber inputs (primary + secondary) for redundancy
Wireless backup connectivity for continuity during fiber outages
2) Tools & Materials
OMEGA ONT + power adapter (with surge protection)
Mounting kit (shelf stand or wall bracket + anchors)
Approved single-mode fiber patch cords
Optical cleaning kit (lint-free wipes, isopropyl alcohol ≥ 90%, connector cleaner)
Cable labels / zip ties / strain-relief clips
Technician laptop or mobile app (for ONT configuration)
Tone tester / optical power meter (if required by policy)
3) Safety & Handling
Eye protection when handling fiber.
Never look into fiber connectors/ports.
Observe minimum bend radius (typically ≥ 30 mm; follow local spec).
Disconnect power before inserting/removing fiber jumpers.
Keep ports and ferrules clean and capped when not in use.
4) Site Assessment & Placement Recommendations
Location: Near the fiber demarc (IDF/media panel/utility closet) inside the home.
Power: Dedicated, grounded outlet; use surge protector.
Environment: Dry, cool, dust-free; avoid HVAC discharge, kitchens, bathrooms, or direct sun.
Accessibility: LEDs and ports visible; allow ≥ 6 in (15 cm) clearance on all sides.
RF considerations (for wireless backup):
Prefer a central, elevated location away from large metal appliances and dense masonry.
Avoid stacking with high-EMI gear (e.g., large amplifiers) if possible.
5) Installation Steps
5.1 Mount & Power
Mount to wall (eye-level) or place on a stable, ventilated shelf.
Route power cable with drip-loop (if near entry point).
Plug into surge protector, but do not power on yet.
5.2 Prep Fiber
Verify fiber type/connector (e.g., SC/APC).
Clean both ONT ports and patch cord ferrules.
Label each patch cord end with destination/port role.
5.3 Connect Redundant Fibers
Insert Primary Fiber → Port 1 (click to seat; no force).
Insert Secondary Fiber → Port 2 (for failover).
Dress fibers with strain relief; maintain bend radius; secure to wall/rail.
5.4 Wireless Backup (if integrated/separate module)
Install or enable wireless module per model instructions.
Position antennas vertically; avoid obstructions.
Configure SSID/credentials or LTE/eSIM profile as required.
5.5 Power-On & Initialization
Apply power; wait for boot/LED stabilization (typically 2–5 min).
Confirm LEDs:
P1 Link: solid/green
P2 Link: solid/green (if lit, redundancy ready)
WAN/Service: solid/green
Wi-Fi/Backup: solid/green or slow pulse when on standby
Refer to your model’s LED legend if colors/patterns differ.
5.6 Provisioning & Validation
Connect via Tech App / Web UI (service laptop or mobile).
Update to approved firmware (if prompted).
Run Provisioning: authenticate device, apply service profile, enable auto-failover (P1→P2→Wireless).
Tests:
Optical levels (Rx/Tx) within spec for P1 and P2
Service ping / throughput test (primary active)
Failover test: Disable P1 (simulate cut) → verify P2 carries traffic; disable P2 → verify wireless backup carries traffic; re-enable P1 and confirm reversion.
Document serial, ONT MAC, port mapping, RSSI (wireless), and speed test results in the work order.
5.7 Customer Handoff
Show the customer the power, fiber, and status LEDs.
Explain automatic redundancy and when wireless may engage.
Provide “Do not move/unplug” guidance and support contact.
6) Diagram — Placement & Connectivity (Mermaid)
Paste the following Mermaid block into a Markdown/Confluence/Miro (Mermaid app) environment to render the diagram..

SOP: Burying Fiber Drops & Handling Cable Damage
1) Purpose
To standardize the process for technicians burying fiber drops and repairing damaged cables during installation or maintenance.

2) Tools & Materials
Fiber drop cable (singlemode, burial-rated)
Conduit (PVC or HDPE, if required)
Shovel or trenching tool
Warning tape and cable markers
Optical cleaning kit (lint-free wipes, ≥90% isopropyl alcohol)
Tone tester / OTDR / optical power meter
Splice kit or pre-connectorized repair kit
Technician laptop or mobile app for provisioning

3) Safety
Call 811 or local utility locate service before digging.
Wear eye protection and gloves.
Maintain minimum bend radius (≥30 mm).
Avoid sharp bends, kinks, or crushing during burial.

4) Burial Guidelines
Depth: 12–18 inches minimum (check local code).
Path: Straight runs; avoid roots, rocks, and high-traffic areas.
Protection: Use conduit under driveways or sidewalks.
Markers: Place warning tape 6 inches above cable in trench.

5) Installation Steps
Plan route and confirm utility clearance.
Dig trench to required depth.
Lay fiber drop cable with gentle curves; maintain bend radius.
Apply strain relief at entry points.
Place warning tape above cable.
Backfill trench carefully; avoid crushing cable.
Test optical levels and provision service.

6) Addressing Cable Damage
Identify damage: Look for visible cuts, severe bends, or signal loss.
Isolate section: Use tone tester or OTDR.
Repair options: 
Minor jacket scuff: Apply protective wrap.
Fiber break: Use splice kit or replace section.
Clean connectors before reconnecting.
Validate repair: Test optical power and service after fix.

7) Documentation
Record burial depth, route, and repair details in work order.
Include serial numbers, optical readings, and photos if required.

Troubleshooting Flow (Quick Reference)
No signal after burial? 
Check bend radius and strain relief.
Inspect for crushed or kinked cable.
Test with OTDR to locate break.
Signal loss after repair? 
Reclean connectors.
Verify splice integrity.
Retest optical levels.
